body:
Global crypto markets opened August on a cautious note, with total market cap sitting at $2.25T, up just +0.14% over 24 hours — barely enough to call it a rally. The broad tape reads sideways to slightly offered, with the Fear & Greed Index locked at 27 for a second consecutive session, a number that tells you most participants are either flat or hedged. Volume came in at $38.4B for the day, which is functional but not the kind of print that signals conviction in either direction. BTC dominance at 56.3% and ETH dominance down to 10.0% suggest rotation pressure underneath the surface, with capital hunting for smaller-cap setups rather than anchoring in majors.

Bitcoin printed $63,087, a session that looked almost deliberately uneventful — +0.20% over 24 hours, -0.50% in the last hour, and -1.80% on the week. The 7-day drift is the number worth watching: BTC has been bleeding slowly without a clean flush, which means there is no obvious capitulation bottom to buy into. Volume at $15.53B is respectable but not the kind of surge that typically accompanies a trend reversal. The security picture complicates the narrative materially: a Coldcard hardware wallet attack has now spread to 4,500 addresses with losses reportedly near $89 million per CoinDesk, and CryptoQuant flagged this as the biggest sub-1 BTC address movement since FTX. That is not background noise — retail cold-storage confidence is the one thing that does not recover quickly once shaken, and any further propagation of that story will weigh on sentiment independent of macro.

The altcoin tape today was the more interesting read. ADA was the standout at +8.50% over 24 hours and +12.50% on the week, with $0.52B in volume — no single catalyst was evident in available headlines, but the momentum is real and the weekly print suggests accumulation rather than a one-day spike. UNI is similarly constructive at +14.60% on the week despite modest 24-hour gains of +2.60%, and DOT added +4.50% in the session. AVAX posted +3.20% on the day but is still -3.00% on the week, so the bounce there looks corrective rather than structural. ETH at $1,863.83 is the quiet underperformer — -0.10% on the day, -0.70% on the week, with $5.45B in volume — and a 10.0% market dominance reading is a level that warrants attention from any ETH-focused book. BNB at $582.36 was the clearest laggard at -1.10% over 24 hours, though its +2.10% weekly print keeps it from looking broken.

The macro backdrop is adding friction across the board. Bitcoin mining difficulty has shrunk 14% from this year's high per CoinDesk, a data point that reflects the margin squeeze operators are facing as revenues decline — historically that kind of miner stress does not resolve quietly. Russia's expanded crypto mining ban now covers Moscow through 2032 per Cointelegraph, removing meaningful hashrate from the legitimate network and adding geopolitical opacity to the supply picture. On the regulatory front, Minnesota's crypto ATM ban went into effect following reported $1M in losses per Cointelegraph, and the Bank of Italy published research questioning whether stablecoins actually deliver cheaper remittances — a headline that matters for anyone modeling stablecoin adoption curves as a base case. The tokenized stock story — 288% surge in July trading per CoinDesk — is a bright spot, though the caveat that a single QQQ token drove most of it means the headline number overstates breadth.

Looking ahead, the Coldcard exploit trajectory is the single highest-priority risk to monitor: if the $89M figure grows or if a major exchange flags exposure, the sentiment overhang could push Fear & Greed below 27 and pressure BTC toward a test of levels not yet established by today's quiet session. A clean break and hold above $64,000 in BTC on meaningful volume would be the first sign that buyers are stepping in with conviction rather than just absorbing passive sell flow. On the opportunity side, ADA and UNI's weekly momentum is worth tracking for continuation — both need to hold their 24-hour gains into tomorrow's open to validate the thesis. The tokenized equities narrative, crypto PAC spending in Michigan per Cointelegraph, and any follow-on commentary from European central bank researchers on stablecoins could each shift institutional positioning at the margin. Until BTC finds a direction with volume behind it, the default assumption remains choppy and mean-reverting.
